order_note: No predecessor and no order on this engine. SQL 110 needs the homeowner ledger tables (homeowner_ledger_tokens, homeowner_ledger_check_uploads, homeowner_ledger_events, from the restored Supabase schema) owned by checksops_admin without FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. Apply it before the API change that deletes pre-claim links or calls public.aws_public_homeowner_ledger_upload: until then a DELETE by checksops fails with permission denied, and the public upload's direct INSERT is refused by aws_write_homeowner_ledger_check_uploads. SQL 110 grants DELETE on homeowner_ledger_tokens to checksops (no policy change: aws_write_homeowner_ledger_tokens, FOR ALL with aws_can_write_tenant, decides which rows) and creates one SECURITY DEFINER function, EXECUTE checksops only. No later migration replaces it.

tooling.note: Guarded tooling for SQL 110: sql110-homeowner-preclaim-links-production-apply.mjs --inspect (read-only) and the receipt-gated --apply on the engine shared with the staging guarded executor (choice sql110-homeowner-preclaim-links); production-sql-one-shot.mjs --migration sql110. intended_replacement_sha256 is the code-derived fingerprint (releaseIntendedHash in release-sql-state.mjs, equal to the staging pin's): the function's language, volatility, SECURITY DEFINER, result, search_path, body hash and EXECUTE ACL (checksops and the owner), and the checksops DELETE line on homeowner_ledger_tokens. The pre-conditions also require that the applying login can write the three homeowner ledger tables as a definer (definer_can_write_relations) and owns homeowner_ledger_tokens; the post-conditions require every other grant on homeowner_ledger_tokens unchanged. The tooling does not authorize anything: this pin stays execute false until a reviewed change records the staging acceptance, the production inspect and an owner approval.
